goals.title: Discover server and trace capabilities
goals.summary: Choose callable analysis capabilities without treating this catalog as the complete WPA universe.

goals.title: Manage trace lifecycle
goals.summary: Load, reuse, and retire principal-scoped immutable trace generations.

goals.title: Inventory execution
goals.summary: Orient by process, thread, and marker evidence before narrowing analysis scope.

goals.title: Find CPU hotspots
goals.summary: Measure sampled CPU stacks and scheduler CPU accounting.

goals.title: Explain waits and readiness
goals.summary: Measure blocked time and associated scheduler stack evidence without overstating causality.

goals.title: Investigate startup
goals.summary: Correlate process creation, image loading, I/O, scheduling, and heuristic scan evidence.

goals.title: Investigate storage I/O
goals.summary: Measure file, disk, and hard-fault activity with explicit stack boundaries.

goals.title: Investigate memory
goals.summary: Measure memory resources, faults, virtual allocation traffic, and heap allocations.

goals.title: Investigate network activity
goals.summary: Measure connection lifecycle and network I/O stack evidence.

goals.title: Investigate .NET runtime
goals.summary: Measure CLR GC, JIT, allocation, exception, contention, and finalizer evidence.

goals.title: Investigate system activity
goals.summary: Inspect registry, ALPC, interrupt, and caller-selected provider stacks.

goals.title: Investigate security activity
goals.summary: Inspect heuristic scan-like activity while preserving scanner-attribution boundaries.

goals.title: Prepare and assess symbols
goals.summary: Separate trace PDB identity, verified local readiness, and measured frame resolution.

goals.title: Correlate a time window
goals.summary: Join bounded cross-domain observations without manufacturing causal conclusions.

goals.title: Validate capture evidence
goals.summary: Assess parser-observed evidence and preserve uncertainty about raw capture completeness.

workflows.title: Capability-first orientation
workflows.summary: Read the declared server map, then evaluate the loaded trace before selecting an analyzer.

workflows.title: Secure trace lifecycle
workflows.summary: Load one immutable generation, run bounded queries, then retire its public handle.

workflows.title: Execution inventory
workflows.summary: Resolve process and thread instances and locate marker anchors before scoped analysis.

workflows.title: CPU hotspot analysis
workflows.summary: Use sampled stacks for code attribution and scheduler events for CPU accounting.

workflows.title: Wait and readiness analysis
workflows.summary: Measure blocked intervals and related readier evidence while keeping causality not concluded.

workflows.title: Startup investigation
workflows.summary: Correlate creation, image, file, scheduler, and scan-like evidence in bounded startup windows.

workflows.title: Storage I/O investigation
workflows.summary: Measure file and disk activity and distinguish hard-fault file attribution from stack evidence.

workflows.title: Memory investigation
workflows.summary: Combine resource snapshots and operation traffic with fault and allocation stack evidence.

workflows.title: Network investigation
workflows.summary: Separate connection lifecycle evidence from byte-weighted network stack evidence.

workflows.title: .NET runtime investigation
workflows.summary: Select only CLR evidence classes actually observed in the trace.

workflows.title: System activity investigation
workflows.summary: Inspect registry, IPC, interrupt, and explicit provider event evidence.

workflows.title: Security activity investigation
workflows.summary: Use heuristic scan evidence as a hypothesis and require authoritative evidence for scanner attribution.

workflows.title: Immutable symbol preparation
workflows.summary: Prepare a policy-bound context and never equate PDB identity or local readiness with frame resolution.

workflows.title: Bounded window correlation
workflows.summary: Correlate available evidence classes in one window and keep unsupported causality explicit.

workflows.title: Capture and parser validation
workflows.summary: Distinguish materialized logical events from unavailable raw-record completeness evidence.

capabilities.title: List the declared server capability map
capabilities.summary: Projects stable goals, workflows, callable tools, evidence boundaries, evaluators, and content-addressed output-contract references from one validated Active Catalog.
questionsAnswered: Which capabilities, workflows, and tools does this validated wpa-mcp build declare?
Which evidence and conclusion boundaries govern each declared capability?
Where can a client retrieve and hash-verify an active tool's complete Contract 2.0 output schema?
questionsNotAnswered: Is this the complete capability universe of WPA, ETW, or every external analyzer?
Does an unlisted capability definitely not exist outside this server?

capabilities.title: Load an immutable trace generation
capabilities.summary: Validates and snapshots an allowed ETL/ETLX source into the server-owned artifact store, then returns the canonical principal-scoped TraceId for its immutable generation.
questionsAnswered: Which canonical principal-scoped TraceId names the loaded immutable trace generation?
Was an existing active handle reused, and what source-generation assurance was applied?
questionsNotAnswered: What other active handles or leases exist for this principal?
Is the retained artifact quota a hard bound on converter-time or whole-root physical peak bytes?

capabilities.title: Retire a principal-scoped trace handle
capabilities.summary: Idempotently retires one canonical TraceId for the current principal, rejects new acquisitions, and optionally waits for active query leases to drain without deleting the independently retained artifact.
questionsAnswered: Was this principal-scoped TraceId retired or already unloaded, and did its active leases drain?
questionsNotAnswered: Was an immutable trace artifact deleted?
What other active handles, leases, or retained artifacts exist?

capabilities.title: Inspect parsed trace evidence
capabilities.summary: Reports parsed trace metadata, provider/event observations, domain stack coverage, and explicit evidence limitations.
questionsAnswered: Which event domains and stack evidence did the parser observe in this trace?
questionsNotAnswered: What was the raw capture event count outside TraceEvent parsing?
Do PDB identities prove that frames were resolved?
Does an unobserved event prove its keyword was disabled?
optionalEvidence: domain event and metric stack coverage

capabilities.title: List process instances
capabilities.summary: Lists resolved process lifetimes for selector orientation, including process-table/rundown backfill that does not prove an observed ProcessStart event.
questionsAnswered: Which parsed process lifetimes can be used to scope later analysis?
questionsNotAnswered: Does a PID alone uniquely identify one lifetime?
Are rows beyond the requested top value included?

capabilities.title: Process creation timing
capabilities.summary: Measures observed child starts for one safely selected parent process lifetime.
questionsAnswered: When were child ProcessStart events observed relative to the selected parent lifetime?
questionsNotAnswered: Which mechanism caused a child-start or first-image gap?
Can a reused parent PID be safely analyzed without its start time?

capabilities.title: Thread lifetime inventory
capabilities.summary: Lists thread generations within a safely selected process lifetime. Whole-trace availability requires at least one fully observed ThreadStart-to-ThreadStop lifetime and no unmatched or inferred-boundary evidence; source-only and rundown-bounded evidence is partial.
questionsAnswered: Which thread generations and observed lifetimes belong to the selected process instance?
questionsNotAnswered: Does a TID alone uniquely identify a thread lifetime?
Does a rundown-only lifetime prove an observed thread creation or termination?
Does lifetime duration explain CPU or wait causality?
optionalEvidence: Thread/DCStart and Thread/DCStop rundown boundary evidence
Structured source, completed, unmatched, and inferred-boundary counts

capabilities.title: Search trace markers
capabilities.summary: Searches parsed event names and payload fields using explicit text filters and bounded output.
questionsAnswered: Which parsed marker-like events match the supplied search mode and text?
questionsNotAnswered: Does a text match establish the marker's application semantics?
Are results complete beyond the requested bound?

capabilities.title: Sampled CPU stack attribution
capabilities.summary: Aggregates sampled-profile stack metrics for explicit trace, process, thread, and time scopes.
questionsAnswered: Which frames account for observed sampled CPU events in the selected scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Does sample share equal exact CPU time?
Are unresolved or unstacked samples attributable to a named function?
Does a top-N list contain every function?

capabilities.title: CSwitch CPU accounting
capabilities.summary: Derives per-thread on-CPU duration from CSwitch intervals; ready latency is exposed only when ReadyThread evidence is present.
questionsAnswered: How much scheduled CPU time was derived from scoped CSwitch evidence, and—when ReadyThread exists—what ready latency was observed?
questionsNotAnswered: Does scheduler time identify the code responsible without stacks?
Can unresolved thread identities be safely assigned?

capabilities.title: Blocked-time accounting
capabilities.summary: Projects CSwitch blocking intervals and wait reasons into the selected process/thread/window scope.
questionsAnswered: How much completed blocked time and which wait reasons were observed in scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Do trace-wide CSwitch counts describe the selected process?
Does a wait reason prove the application root cause?

capabilities.title: Blocking-stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks switch-out stacks associated with completed blocked intervals in the selected scope.
questionsAnswered: Which switch-out frames are associated with observed scoped blocked duration?
questionsNotAnswered: Does the associated stack prove the causal root of the wait?
Do stacks from another thread establish scoped stack availability?

capabilities.title: ReadyThread readier-stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks recorded on ReadyThread events associated with an awakened process scope.
questionsAnswered: Which readier stacks are associated with ReadyThread events for the selected awakened process?
questionsNotAnswered: Who causally unblocked the target thread?
Does temporal/readier association prove the blocking resource or root cause?

capabilities.title: File I/O aggregation
capabilities.summary: Aggregates parsed file read/write byte traffic by temporally resolved file identity.
questionsAnswered: Which resolved file identities account for observed scoped FileIO byte traffic?
questionsNotAnswered: Is every FileObject/FileKey mapping unambiguous?
Does byte traffic equal disk traffic or application latency?

capabilities.title: File I/O stack attribution
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by scoped FileIO events using exact integer byte metrics.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with stacked FileIO byte traffic in scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Do stacks exist for all FileIO events?
Does file I/O imply physical disk access?

capabilities.title: Physical disk I/O aggregation
capabilities.summary: Aggregates physical DiskIO requests, service-time intervals, process lifetimes, disks, and temporally resolved file identities without requiring event stacks.
questionsAnswered: Which processes, files, and physical disks account for observed scoped DiskIO requests and bytes?
What read/write, service-time, and bounded busy-time trends were observed in the selected window?
questionsNotAnswered: Does disk busy percentage alone prove storage saturation or root cause?
Did an I/O whose completion event falls outside the selected window contribute busy time inside it?
Is every DiskIO FileKey mapping unambiguous?

capabilities.title: Disk I/O stack attribution
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by physical disk I/O events using exact byte metrics.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with observed stacked disk byte traffic?
questionsNotAnswered: Do stacks exist for every disk event?
Does association identify the ultimate performance cause?

capabilities.title: Hard faults by file
capabilities.summary: Aggregates observed hard faults by temporally resolved file identity.
questionsAnswered: Which resolved files account for observed scoped hard faults?
questionsNotAnswered: Is every historical FileKey mapping unambiguous?
Do hard faults prove a memory leak or storage root cause?

capabilities.title: Hard-fault stack attribution
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by observed hard-fault events.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with stacked hard-fault events and bytes?
questionsNotAnswered: Do stacks exist for every hard fault?
Does a stack prove the cause of memory pressure?

capabilities.title: VirtualAlloc operation stacks
capabilities.summary: Ranks VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree operation stacks and separates allocation, free, and operation-volume metrics.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with virtual-memory allocation and free operation volume?
questionsNotAnswered: Does total operation volume equal net committed growth?
Do observed operations prove retained memory?

capabilities.title: Memory resource activity
capabilities.summary: Aggregates four independent facets: per-process memory samples, system-memory snapshots, handle events, and pool events. Any subset is partial; only observation of all four event families makes the aggregate capability available.
questionsAnswered: What memory-resource activity was observed for the selected process instances and window?
questionsNotAnswered: Does event activity equal a point-in-time working set or leak?
Can missing event classes be treated as zero usage?
optionalEvidence: Per-facet event requirements and missing-event warnings

capabilities.title: Image-load timing
capabilities.summary: Lists image-load events and observed timing gaps for one process lifetime.
questionsAnswered: When were image loads observed and what gaps separate them for the selected process instance?
questionsNotAnswered: Did the image load itself consume the preceding gap?
Can reused PID lifetimes be merged safely?

capabilities.title: Image-load stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by scoped image-load events.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with stacked image-load events?
questionsNotAnswered: Do stacks exist for every image load?
Does association prove startup delay causality?

capabilities.title: Network I/O stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by scoped TCP/UDP send and receive events.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with stacked network byte events?
questionsNotAnswered: Does event association prove remote latency or connection causality?
Do stacks cover every network event?

capabilities.title: Network connection event inventory
capabilities.summary: Reconstructs parsed TCP connection lifecycles from Connect/Accept and Disconnect/Reconnect endpoints with exact string connection identifiers. Source-only, unmatched, identity-unresolved, or trace/process-bounded lifecycles are partial; it does not consume Send/Recv byte events.
questionsAnswered: Which connection identifiers and endpoints were observed in the selected scope?
questionsNotAnswered: How many bytes were sent or received?
What throughput was achieved?
Does connection activity prove remote service latency or causality?
Can a deprecated unsafe numeric identifier be treated as authoritative?
optionalEvidence: Structured source, completed, unmatched, and bounded lifecycle counts
Separate network.io.stacks capability for Send/Recv byte evidence

capabilities.title: Registry event stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by registry operation events in the selected scope.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with observed stacked registry operations?
questionsNotAnswered: Does stack association establish policy or root-cause attribution?
Do stacks cover every registry event?

capabilities.title: ALPC event stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by observed ALPC send/receive events.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with stacked ALPC operations?
questionsNotAnswered: Does stack association identify the peer or causal blocker?
Do stacks cover every ALPC event?

capabilities.title: Interrupt/DPC stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by observed ISR and DPC events over a trace window.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with stacked ISR/DPC activity?
questionsNotAnswered: Does stack association prove a device or driver root cause?
Can interrupt events be attributed to a process PID?

capabilities.title: Generic provider stack association
capabilities.summary: Filters one explicitly named provider/event family and ranks stacks carried by matching events.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with matching events from the explicitly selected provider?
questionsNotAnswered: Does name filtering establish event semantics or causality?
Does the parser cover every provider payload?

capabilities.title: Heap allocation stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by heap allocation events and exact allocation byte metrics.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with observed heap allocation traffic?
questionsNotAnswered: Do allocation bytes equal retained bytes or a leak?
Do stacks cover every allocation?

capabilities.title: CLR GC interval accounting
capabilities.summary: Pairs GCStart/GCStop and GCSuspendEEStart/GCRestartEEStop streams. Source-only, unmatched, identity-unresolved, or invalid endpoint evidence is partial; GCHeapStats snapshots do not enable this capability.
questionsAnswered: What GC wall and pause durations were derived from paired CLR endpoints in scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Do unmatched endpoints form complete intervals?
Does a projected interval equal full interval duration?
optionalEvidence: Structured source, completed, unmatched, and boundary counts

capabilities.title: CLR GC heap statistics
capabilities.summary: Uses only GCHeapStats events to report heap snapshots for selected process instances and windows; GC interval endpoints do not enable this capability.
questionsAnswered: Which GC heap-stat values were observed in the selected scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Do sparse snapshots prove continuous heap growth or a leak?
Does absence prove the event keyword was disabled?

capabilities.title: CLR JIT interval accounting
capabilities.summary: Pairs JIT start/load endpoints and reports complete method-compilation intervals projected into scope. A lone start/load, unmatched endpoints, unresolved identities, or invalid ordering yields partial evidence rather than availability.
questionsAnswered: Which completed JIT intervals and durations were observed in scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Do unmatched endpoints represent completed compilations?
Does projected duration equal the full interval?
optionalEvidence: Structured source, completed, unmatched, and boundary counts

capabilities.title: CLR allocation stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by CLR allocation-tick events using exact byte metrics.
questionsAnswered: Which frames and managed types are associated with observed CLR allocation traffic?
questionsNotAnswered: Do sampled allocation ticks equal all allocations or retained memory?
Do stacks cover every allocation event?

capabilities.title: CLR exception stack association
capabilities.summary: Ranks stacks carried by CLR exception events and reports exception-type observations.
questionsAnswered: Which frames and exception types are associated with observed CLR exception events?
questionsNotAnswered: Does an exception event prove failure impact or causal root?
Do stacks cover every exception?

capabilities.title: CLR contention stack association
capabilities.summary: Pairs managed contention intervals and ranks associated start stacks with full/projected duration accounting.
questionsAnswered: Which frames are associated with completed CLR contention duration in scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Does an associated contention stack prove the owner or causal blocker?
Do unmatched endpoints form completed contention?

capabilities.title: CLR finalizer activity
capabilities.summary: Uses the fixed GCFinalizeObject and GCFinalizersStart/Stop event set, reporting object points, batch endpoints, and valid completed batch pairs as distinct evidence in a process/window scope.
questionsAnswered: How many GCFinalizeObject point events were observed in scope?
How many GCFinalizersStart/Stop endpoints were observed in scope?
Which valid completed finalizer batches could be paired and projected into scope?
questionsNotAnswered: Do finalizer counts prove a leak?
Do unmatched endpoints represent a completed batch?

capabilities.title: Configure process symbol path
capabilities.summary: Mutates the process-wide _NT_SYMBOL_PATH legacy configuration.
questionsAnswered: What opaque symbol path string is configured after the mutation?
questionsNotAnswered: Are PDB files reachable, trusted, or correct?
Were any stack frames resolved?

capabilities.title: Add a symbol server configuration
capabilities.summary: Creates or reuses a cache directory and appends a trusted server entry to process-wide symbol configuration.
questionsAnswered: What symbol-path configuration is in effect after adding the server entry?
questionsNotAnswered: Was the remote server contacted now?
Are symbols correct or frames resolved?

capabilities.title: Local symbol metadata diagnostics
capabilities.summary: Reports trace PDB identities and direct local PDB candidate-read evidence without resolving frames.
questionsAnswered: Which modules carry PDB identity and which eligible local candidate PDB files pass direct format/GUID/Age checks?
questionsNotAnswered: What percentage of stack frames resolve to function names?
Are remote symbols available?

capabilities.title: Scan-like security event heuristics
capabilities.summary: Classifies supported security-provider events and explicit scan-like name patterns with provenance and confidence.
questionsAnswered: Which recognized or heuristic scan-like observations matched the requested filters?
questionsNotAnswered: Was a specific antivirus product certainly scanning the target?
Did scan-like activity cause a performance delay?
requiredEvents: Supported security provider events or explicit scan-like names

capabilities.title: Bounded window evidence composite
capabilities.summary: Combines scoped CPU, scheduler, wait, and stack observations for one bounded window or compares one exact thread instance across named windows.
questionsAnswered: What selected CPU/wait evidence was observed in this bounded process/window scope?
How do sampled CPU, running, ready latency, and blocked duration differ across named windows for one exact thread instance?
questionsNotAnswered: Does the composite prove one causal root?
Are skipped, failed, or top-N sections complete?
Do a wait reason or switch-out stack prove the responsible blocking method when stack coverage or symbols are missing?
requiredEvents: Sampled profile and scheduler events when available

capabilities.title: High-wait candidate composite
capabilities.summary: Selects process-lifetime wait candidates and conditionally gathers blocking and ReadyThread stack associations within a budget.
questionsAnswered: Which considered process instances have high observed wait ratios and what associated evidence was gathered?
questionsNotAnswered: Does a candidate or readier stack prove causal responsibility?
Were candidates outside bounded input evaluated?

capabilities.title: Slow-startup evidence composite
capabilities.summary: Ranks a bounded set of observed startup process instances and gathers CPU, wait, image-load, and window evidence.
questionsAnswered: Which considered startup instances have the largest observed startup wall/wait evidence?
questionsNotAnswered: Does the selected evidence prove a startup root cause?
Were startup instances beyond the candidate-input cap evaluated?

capabilities.title: Mechanistic unblock causality
capabilities.summary: A future capability requiring paired mechanistic evidence before identifying a causal unblock source.
questionsAnswered: Can mechanistic paired evidence establish who caused an unblock?
questionsNotAnswered: Can a ReadyThread readier stack alone establish causality?

capabilities.title: Verified scanner attribution
capabilities.summary: A future capability requiring authoritative provider/product identity and target linkage.
questionsAnswered: Can evidence authoritatively attribute a scan to a named scanner and target?
questionsNotAnswered: Can event-name heuristics prove scanner identity?
requiredEvents: Authoritative scanner identity and target linkage

capabilities.title: Measured frame resolution
capabilities.summary: A future explicit symbol-context capability that measures successful frame-to-function lookup.
questionsAnswered: What fraction of eligible stack frames actually resolved under one immutable symbol context?
questionsNotAnswered: Can PDB identity or local-file presence substitute for frame lookup?

capabilities.title: External raw capture count
capabilities.summary: A future capability that reports a raw capture count with provenance distinct from parser-observed events.
questionsAnswered: How many raw records does an external capture-level counter report, and under which counting basis?
questionsNotAnswered: Can TraceEvent parsed-event counts be relabeled as raw capture totals?

capabilities.title: Cross-domain causal attribution
capabilities.summary: A future conclusion-rule capability requiring mechanistic, scoped, complete cross-domain evidence.
questionsAnswered: Does named mechanistic evidence support a causal cross-domain conclusion?
questionsNotAnswered: Can temporal correlation or shared PID alone establish causality?

capabilities.title: Prepare immutable symbol context
capabilities.summary: Prepares or reuses a principal-scoped immutable SymbolContextId from startup-approved local policy and verified pinned artifacts.
questionsAnswered: Which immutable symbol context can be referenced by later analysis without hidden symbol I/O?
questionsNotAnswered: Can process-global symbol path mutation substitute for an immutable context?

capabilities.title: Principal-scoped trace handle
capabilities.summary: Registry-backed TraceId creation, acquisition, and retirement are implemented through load/query/unload operations; this remains a gap because no independent callable handle-status or inventory surface exposes a capability-keyed runtime outcome.
questionsAnswered: Can the current MCP surface independently inspect the state of a principal-scoped TraceId?
questionsNotAnswered: Which handles, leases, expiry states, and immutable generations are currently active for this principal?
Can load_trace or unload_trace results substitute for an independent handle-status snapshot?

capabilities.title: Trace artifact physical peak hard bound
capabilities.summary: Release-blocked gap: retained quotas and serialized materialization checkpoint budgets are enforced, but the whole-root physical peak is not hard-bounded because TraceLog converter transient space is opaque.
questionsAnswered: Is the configured artifact-store byte limit a proven hard bound on the whole artifact root's physical peak?
questionsNotAnswered: What exact maximum transient space can TraceLog.OpenOrConvert consume between observable checkpoints?
Can MaxArtifactStoreBytes be presented as a whole-operation or whole-root physical peak cap?
optionalEvidence: Retained byte and object quota enforcement
Independent worker or filesystem quota proof
